_about: Real program history the app's writers (group chat, dispatch, campus feed) are given as facts, so they never have to guess. WYO was researched by hand; a school you start coaching later is fetched from Wikipedia automatically ("auto": true, "reviewed": false) - look it over and edit freely. What your dynasty does (title games, finished seasons) is added from the save.

facts: Before this dynasty, the last time Wyoming played for a conference title was the 2016 Mountain West Championship Game, a 27-24 home loss to San Diego State in Laramie; the last time it won one was 1993, in the WAC.
Wyoming has won 14 conference championships: seven in the Skyline Conference (1949, 1950, 1956, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961) and seven in the WAC (1966, 1967, 1968, 1976, 1987, 1988, 1993).
Wyoming's last conference title was in 1993, in the WAC. It has never won a Mountain West title since joining the conference in 1999.
Wyoming's previous Mountain West Championship Game was in 2016: the Cowboys hosted it in Laramie and lost 27-24 to San Diego State.
In 1996 Wyoming won the WAC's Pacific division and lost the WAC Championship Game.
The 1967 Cowboys went 10-0 in the regular season and played LSU in the 1968 Sugar Bowl, losing 20-13; they peaked at No. 5, still the highest ranking in program history.
Home games are at War Memorial Stadium in Laramie, the highest stadium in major college football (about 7,220 feet).
Before this dynasty, Wyoming had never played in the College Football Playoff.
Before this dynasty, Wyoming's most recent postseason win was the 2023 Arizona Bowl: 16-15 over Toledo on a field goal as time expired, Craig Bohl's last game as coach.
The Texas Longhorns football program represents the University of Texas at Austin in American football.
It is part of the wider Longhorns athletics program and competes at the NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) level as a member of the Southeastern Conference.
Home stadium: Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas (capacity 100,119).
Rivals: Arkansas; Baylor; Oklahoma; Rice; TCU; Texas A&M; Texas Tech.
Fight song: Texas Fight; mascot: Bevo.
